what_happened.line: The Water District board agreed to draft a letter or memorandum stating its position on lake-impact concerns, for use when the issue is raised again.
Most of the meeting covered Conservation Commission concerns about the Hickory Hills pilot test, including fencing, security, a dry well and remediation.
Members discussed getting prices for temporary and permanent fencing, with a minimal fence proposed if the issue continues.
The board reviewed its long-term debt schedule and how loans dropping off could be applied to payments on the Mass Ave water main loan.
The loan term for the Mass Ave main, compared at 10, 15 and 20 years, is to be chosen after temporary borrowing. No votes were recorded except adjournment.

why_it_matters: Water district debt is paid through customer bills, so how the Mass Ave main is financed, and whether any difference appears as a line item on bills, bears on what water users pay.
The letter on lake-impact concerns would set the district's written position on the Hickory Hills pilot test, which affects how the question is handled with the Conservation Commission.
